subject: Post-demo: head-to-head snapshot & validation asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: head-to-head snapshot & validation asks

Alex — thanks for your time today. Quick write-up from our call to make sure we’re all aligned and to capture the tests you flagged. I’ve attached the head-to-head criteria workbook and the recording for the session.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Latency variance for live inference under bursty traffic (primary)
- Cost per inference for high-throughput nightly jobs (secondary)
- On-prem / VPC controls and KMS integration for PHI-sensitive payloads

Goals you shared:
1) Achieve predictable 95th-percentile latency <= 250ms for 1–2k QPS sustained for common clinical prompts.
2) Keep per-API-call cost reduction of >= 30% vs current vendor for production workloads.
3) Validate security posture (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) for procurement.

Decision criteria we captured (prioritized):
- Latency (P95) under expected QPS
- Model parity on clinical prompts (accuracy & hallucination profile)
- Deployment options (hosted vs VPC vs on-prem) and key management
- Cost/run rate at target throughput

Requested next-step experiments we propose from our side:
1) Latency sweep: run 3 load profiles (100 QPS, 500 QPS, 1.5k QPS) with your sample dataset and capture P50/P95/P99 and token-level cost.
2) Model parity: side-by-side generation comparison across your 20 canonical prompts + 50 anonymized clinical notes; we’ll deliver a blind scoring sheet.
3) Security review: provide SOC2 attestation + KMS options; offer a short architecture whiteboard session for your infra team.

Asks for MedSync to unblock the tests:
- Confirm a contact who can share the anonymized sample dataset (S3 link or secure Drive).
- Confirm the expected QPS target and peak bursts you anticipate for the demo tests.
- Any non-disclosure / procurement gating documents we should sign before full dataset transfer.

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- By Oct 6: we’ll send a test matrix and the exact upload instructions.
- Week of Oct 12: run latency & parity tests.
- Oct 20: readout + decision check-in.

If that aligns, we’ll prepare the test plan and SOC2 artifacts for your security team.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the test matrix later today.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: redwood-headtohead-criteria.xlsx; demo-recording.mp4
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsynchealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@medsynchealth.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: head-to-head snapshot & validation asks

Thanks, Soojin — this is a great summary and matches what the team heard. Quick additions from our side: we have a procurement checkpoint on Oct 18 where the security packet needs to be in place for exec review.

A few clarifications: 
- Our primary target for day-1 P95 is 250ms for the “Clinical Triage” prompt set at 1k sustained QPS, with brief bursts up to 1.8k.
- For parity scoring, we’ll anonymize 50 notes and a canonical set of 20 prompts — I’ll route the dataset to your secure bucket once we have an NDA in place.
- SOC2 is required; we also need evidence of customer-managed KMS support and retention/audit-log behavior for 90 days.

Procurement timeline: 
- Oct 6: security confirms required artifacts list
- Oct 12–15: run tests
- Oct 18: procurement/security readout
- Oct 25: target decision window for pilot approval

I’ve attached our internal evaluation checklist (medsync-eval-criteria.pdf) — it maps to our scoring weights. Also looping Priya (head of platform) for the dataset hand-off.

Alex Johnson
Director of Platform Engineering
MedSync Health
alex.johnson@medsynchealth.com
Attachments: medsync-eval-criteria.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsynchealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: head-to-head snapshot & validation asks

Appreciate the timeline — that works. A few concrete notes to address the SOC2/KMS/retention asks and the test mechanics so procurement has what it needs: 

Security/compliance answers (summary):
- SOC2: we’ll share the current SOC2 Type II attestation and the control matrix by Oct 6.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and can provision HSM-based flows for Private deployments; we’ll outline the integration steps in the packet.
- Audit logs: 90-day retention is supported in our Console; we can provide event export (immutable) for the window you requested.

Test plan (we’ll send full matrix as an attachment):
- Latency sweep: 3 profiles (100/500/1500 QPS) with burst window (1.8k) — we’ll capture P50/P95/P99, token cost, and tail jitter samples.
- Parity: blind A/B across 3 model variants (open-1, open-2-quant, redwood-optimized-7b) with scoring by your SMEs.
- Environment: prefer to run on a dedicated lane (isolated capacity) so the P95 numbers are representative; we can run an initial hosted test and then repeat in a dedicated sandbox if needed.

Asks from MedSync to proceed:
- An S3 or secure Drive link with the anonymized sample dataset + a short README describing expected throughput per prompt (format & QPS profile).
- Confirmation you’re OK signing our mutual NDA (link below) prior to dataset transfer.

I attached a compact test matrix CSV so you can see the exact metrics we’ll capture (headtohead-test-matrix.csv). If you prefer different QPS points or an extra model candidate, say so and we’ll adapt.

We’ll also include a short whiteboard session for Priya and the platform team to walk KMS integration next week.

Best,
Soojin

Looping in a quick commercial note so procurement has context on pricing expectations for a dedicated lane POC: 

- Short POC (2 weeks, dedicated lane): we typically offer a trial credit that covers baseline infra for the test; incremental usage above baseline billed at list rates.
- Pilot pricing guidance (indicative): reserved burst lane discounts available at commitment >= 3 months; typical enterprise pilot discounts range 10–25% depending on capacity and support SLA.
- If MedSync is targeting Oct 25 decision, we should prepare a one-page pilot pricing term and an optional extension at a pre-negotiated rate.

Soojin — can you confirm the baseline capacity we should provision for the POC (I’m assuming 1k sustained QPS with bursts to 1.8k) so I can draft numbers? Also flag any special procurement asks (SOW, PO cadence) we should bake into the one-pager.

Thanks — Marissa
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marissa — that approach sounds reasonable. We’d like the POC to be scoped exactly as you outlined: 2-week dedicated lane, baseline 1k sustained QPS, 1.8k burst for 30s windows. Priya will coordinate the dataset and the legal team will route the NDA.

Open asks before we start: 
- Can Redwood run the POC against a model variant that uses quantized weights (open-2-quant) so we can validate cost/latency trade-offs?
- Please include a brief runbook that shows how we can promote the config to a longer reserved lane if the pilot is successful.

I’ll expect the test matrix and SOC2 packet by Oct 6 so our security folks can review ahead of the Oct 12 run.

Alex
